name: Ventureño Chumash
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Applegate, Richard. 1973. A Sketch of Ventureño Chumash. Rough-draft manuscript, 257 pp. (with 1999 introductory note). California Language Archive, Applegate.001 (https://berkeley.app.box.com/v/applegate-001).
catalog_locator: Chapter 2 (200 Phonology/Phonetics; 220 Comments on articulatory phonetics), sec. 226 'Stress', ms. page 2-11 of the CLA scan
catalog_quote: 226 Stress. Stress is distinctive in a few stems, [where] it falls on the stem-final syllable, as in waqsík 'to paint', c̓ohóy 'other, another one', xalašát 'San Nicholas Island' [handwritten: qaláw 'to detach']. Otherwise stress is non-distinctive, [and] JPH seldom bothered to mark it. [Stress] falls on the penultimate syllable of the word, after the application of all phonological rules. /ka-c-iy-ulu-aq-pey-us/ kasiyuleqpéyus 'they follow him', /loʔ-ka-c-kokoʔ/ loʔkaskókoʔ 'her father', /heʔ-si-ʔoʔ/ heʔsóʔo 'the water', /si-šɨpɨš-iwaš/ ʔišɨpɨšíwaš 'wise one'. When a final vowel is broken with a glottal stop, forming two distinct syllables, stress falls on the first of these [handwritten: — the penultimate syllable in the word]. yɨláʔa 'all', ʔatapl̓íʔiš 'the east', /k-waš-nal̓-Vš/ kwašnal̓íʔiš 'something [which] I hold out'.

It is headed '2-11' (handwritten) and '226 Stress', exactly the locator given. The typed text with hand corrections reads: 'Stress is [marked, struck] distinctive in a few stems, [in which -> hand: where] it falls on the stem-final syllable, as in waqsík 'to paint', - c̓ohóy 'other, another one', - xalašát 'San Nicholas Island'' with handwritten 'qaláw to detach' added at right (and a struck hand entry '..to know, be aware'); '[But, struck] Otherwise stress is [unmarked, struck] non-distinctive, [hand: and] JPH seldom bothered to mark it, [hand: Stress] falls on the penultimate syllable…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is predictable and non-contrastive: it falls on the penultimate syllable of the surface word (computed after all phonological rules). A word-final vowel 'broken' by a glottal stop (VʔV) counts as two syllables, so stress lands on the vowel before the ʔ. A small set of stems are lexical exceptions with stem-final (word-final) stress.
new_statements.exceptions: A few stems carry distinctive stem-final stress: waqšík 'to paint', c̓ohóy 'other', xalašát 'San Nicholas Island', qaláw 'to detach' (hand-added). Author notes Harrington 'seldom bothered to mark' stress otherwise, i.e. the penult default is partly inferred from sparse marking plus Applegate's Ineseño experience.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the (polysynthetic) word including prefixes and suffixes, surface form after phonological rules; examples are elicited words/short phrases from Harrington's 1913-1922 notes (no living speakers; no phrase-level discussion).
new_statements.identity_note: Applegate 1973 describes Ventureño as a whole from J. P. Harrington's 1913-1922 notes (mainly the coast/mission dialect, speaker Fernando Librado; Applegate notes the notes may mix in Cruzeño and Castac forms). Same language as Glottolog vent1242 / ISO veo; Henry-Rodriguez's name for it is Mitsqanaqan̓.
